newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close strong on winter concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close strong on winter concerns.

text.p: Installing a premium in February to cover possible problems from winter weather and continued current feedlot marketings made for a strong close in CME live cattle futures. Feeders followed with technicals and lower corn futures adding to their advance, traders said.

"We have not really put in a winter premium into the February (livestock) contracts yet and that's what we are beginning to do right now," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron trading corp.
Live cattle closed up 1.25 to 0.550 cent, with Febraury up most and December up least at 67.100 cents a lb.

Rolling of long December positions into February by funds kept a lid on December's gains despite expectations cash cattle prices would remain firm in the $68 per cwt area. Feedlots are very current in their marketings and they have no reason to push cattle off of feed, especially since some packers appear short of slaughter supplies, traders said.
Refco and Merrill Lynch bought February and sold December while Rosenthal Collins bought April and June and sold February. R.J. O'Brien and RBH notably bought December early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was general liquidation in December by selling 67 and 68 calls. Volatility was steady in December and February, pit sources added.

Feeders showed spillover support from live cattle as well as scattered demand prompted by lower corn futures. Lower feed costs and possibly firmer fed cattle markets should keep demand for replacement feeder strong, traders said.

Although the latest CME feeder cattle index showed a $0.92 per cwt setback, feeder prices are seen rising. The latest index was based on holiday trade and should turn back up when better quality feeders are marketed, they said.
The market also looked technically strong after penetrating both the 10-day and 20-day averages recently and reaching nearly two week highs, they added.
Cargill Investor Services was a notable buyer while E.D. & F. Man sold. Refco notably bought May. Stone Traders and Cargill spread long January feeders/short June live cattle, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.750 to 0.475 cent higher, with January up most at 66.900 cents.
